more_info.banned_in:
Approved in the EU.
EU permitted levels and categories were reduced from 2013; no US food-colour listing was verified in 2026.
more_info.overview: Ponceau 4R is a red azo food colour. It is also called Cochineal Red A or New Coccine. Its colour comes from a manufactured dye rather than the insect extract used for carmine. The specified colour is supplied as reddish powder or granules.
more_info.origin: Synthetic. Diazotised naphthionic acid is coupled with a naphthol disulfonic acid, and the product is converted to its sodium salt.
more_info.daily_intake: 0.7 mg/kg body weight per day (EFSA, 2009). JECFA allocated 0–4 mg/kg body weight per day in 1983; the assessments differ.
more_info.side_effects:
At food-use levels, limited evidence did not firmly establish this dye alone as a cause of intolerance or behavioural effects. EFSA's refined 2015 exposure assessment found no ADI exceedance after EU limits were reduced.
Kidney changes in a long-term mouse study were used to derive the ADI. This animal finding is not evidence of the same effect at ordinary human food intakes.
more_info.uses:
Examples in the EU food-use list include certain other confectionery including breath freshening microsweets; chewing gum; decorations, coatings and fillings, except fruit-based fillings covered by category 4.2.4; flavoured drinks; flavoured fermented milk products including heat-treated products; non-heat–treated meat products.
The entries apply to particular food categories and may limit the amount, the preparation or the way it is used; they do not show how often the additive appears in retail products.
